item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is materially closer to the frozen contract and has much better scope discipline. Its main defect is that Upload duplicates Add instead of delegating to it, but that is a small, localized correction. B has the same defect while also changing generic retry and request-body ownership semantics explicitly outside the requested scope.","reasons":["Both implementations add the exact Upload signature, validate empty filenames and nil readers, use multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", ...), and produce a replayable buffered multipart body.","A confines production behavior changes to FilesService and preserves Add behavior. B modifies RawClient.Do for every seekable request body, affecting Files.Update, Persons.AddPicture, and other callers despite the contract forbidding unrelated retry refactoring.","Both Upload implementations violate the explicit requirement to route through FilesService.Add; they duplicate its option handling, Raw.Do call, response decoding, and missing-data error instead. A is preferable because fixing this only requires replacing that duplicated block with s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...).","A directly verifies multipart filename/content and that the encoded file content survives a 429 retry. B provides broader validation coverage, but its additional seekable-body tests primarily verify behavior that the contract says not to introduce—not the requested convenience path alone."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add rather than delegating to it, creating future drift in option, request, decoding, and error semantics.","The added tests do not explicitly cover empty-filename validation, nil content, or propagation of a failing source reader.","The extra Add non-replayable-body test and extensive documentation are somewhat beyond the narrow implementation, though they do not change behavior."],"risks_b":["The RawClient.Do seekable-body machinery is a prohibited scope expansion and changes retry behavior SDK-wide.","Wrapping seekable bodies with a no-op Close changes caller-visible ownership semantics and may affect existing integrations that relied on transport closure.","GetBody instances share and mutate one io.ReadSeeker, introducing fragile coupling around retries, redirects, or concurrent body consumption instead of using the established buffered helper path for this feature alone and delegating to Add afterward for the request itself, as the contract requires. This also risks races or corrupt replay if GetBody is invoked while another consumer is active, unlike independent replay readers from buffered content. Additionally, seeking to determine size can mutate reader position on partial seek failures, and the implementation silently leaves the request non-replayable without surfacing the cause, increasing complexity in generic request construction. The broader implementation therefore creates maintenance and behavioral risk far beyond Files.Upload, whereas the contract deliberately chose in-memory buffering through multipartbody.NewFile and existing Add semantics. It also adds substantial tests and changelog claims for Files.Update and Persons.AddPicture behavior that were not requested, making review and rollback harder. Finally, although it tests validation, it still does not explicitly test source-reader failure propagation, so the extra scope does not close all requested test coverage gaps."]}
